newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Pacific merger bodes well for 1997 profit.
newsitem.headline: Pacific merger bodes well for 1997 profit.

text.p: Appliance retailer Pacific Retail Ltd expects to see a "significant" profit improvement in 1997 as a result of its recent merger with unlisted Bond and Bond, Managing Director Greg Lancaster said on Tuesday.
"We'd identified that things were going to have to change in the structure of the retail appliance industry," Lancaster told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"The merger with Bond and Bond goes a long way towards achieving that rationalisation and gives us access to economies of scale that will obviously improve our profitability significantly," he said.
Pacific, formally Noel Leeming, announced in June last year that it would unite with Bond and Bond, but Lancaster said the actual merger had not taken effect until late in 1996.
"The merger only took place in September in terms of signing contracts, but in terms of actually getting the merger in place, that's only happened late November, early December," he said.
"So the first quarter of 1997 will be a good indicator of how we're travelling."
Asked if the company was expecting to seen improved profits by the first quarter of 1997, Lancaster replied: "Yes, we are."
Pacific reported a net profit of NZ$878,000 for the six months to September 30, 1996, down from $1.7 million in the previous corresponding period.
Lancaster said the recent Christmas holiday sales had picked up very late but December receipts had been "acceptable" and the company had met its budget.
"December was acceptable. We didn't come away excited, didn't come away depressed," he said.
"We're comfortable with that, but I think sales between Christmas and New Year weren't quite as strong as they were last year and I suspect that consumer demand at retail is still weak probably."
However, the larger economic picture was promising for the retail sector.

"You'd have to be optimistic about the macroeconomic situation going forward and obviously we'll enjoy some of that, but we're not going to see the booms, I don't believe, that we saw in the 1994, early 1995 period."
Pacific announced in December that a deal to securitise its hire purchase contracts would give it a one-off lift of $3.0 million and lift pre-tax earnings by about $2.3 million annually.
Noel Leeming posted a profit of $2.07 million for the year to March 31, 1996, down from $6.2 million a year earlier.
